name: 蔡坦欣
objective:
本課程提供學生及職前專業人士必備之英語文語言技巧，強調工程專業領域之英文溝通能力之訓練。課程內容依學院專業內容區分並整合英語文之聽說讀寫之能力為未來全球化移動及以英語專業溝通人才培育為目標。
This course aims to provide pre-service engineering students / professionals with the adequate skills of the English language and communicative competence to facilitate their current academic and future career pursuits. Students are encouraged to utilize their domain expertise to participate in professional communication in English. Centered on the training of professional use of the English language, the ESP curriculum as the crux of a highly-integrated work of domain knowledge and the English learning development embodies the indispensable credentials required for a global profession.
schedule:
The following schedule may be adjusted according to students’ learning needs, actual teaching progress, class performance, and the university calendar.

Main course reading: selected Capstone Units 1–3 before the midterm, followed by the selected readings and exercises below. BESTEP activities support visual explanation, summarising and presentation practice.

Week 1 (07 Sep–13 Sep 2026): Orientation, diagnostic tasks and learning resources.

Week 2 (14 Sep–20 Sep 2026): Capstone Unit 1 Big Data: reading, vocabulary and applications.

Week 3 (21 Sep–27 Sep 2026): Unit 1 consolidation and professional speaking practice.

Week 4 (28 Sep–04 Oct 2026): 28 September: Teachers’ Day holiday.

Week 5 (05 Oct–11 Oct 2026): Unit 2 applications and consolidation; review of Units 1–2.

Week 6 (12 Oct–18 Oct 2026): Units 1–2 review and speaking practice.

Week 7 (19 Oct–25 Oct 2026): 19 October: Capstone Unit 3 Robotics, selected reading; thesis-statement writing.

Week 8 (26 Oct–01 Nov 2026): 26 October: university holiday.

Week 9 (2–8 November 2026): Midterm examination week; university common English examination on 3 November. Midterm essay requirements follow the original Classroom task.

Week 10 (9–15 November 2026): 9 November: university holiday; optional Capstone Unit 3 Robotics review.

Week 11 (16–22 November 2026): 16 November: asynchronous Robotics and Internet Security preparation.
Activity: Unit 3 Learning Record Q1–14 and Unit 4 Q1–12; NotebookLM materials, Unit 4 response link and completion check, following the Classroom instructions and deadlines.

Week 12 (23 November 2026): Capstone Unit 4 Hackers and Internet Security.
Activity: source-checking workshop, security timeline/poster, a 60–90-second explanation and Q&A; Learning Record Q13–14 and self-assessment 1.

Week 13 (30 November 2026): Capstone Unit 6 DNA Testing and Family History.
Activity: handwritten personal-data argument in a public discussion thread (150–180 words); transitions, attribution and peer review.

Week 14 (7 December 2026): Capstone Unit 6 writing revision; Style worksheet Part H.
Activity: revise an 80–120-word extract using the three-sentence procedure, check sources with NotebookLM and evaluate Gemini feedback; a 60–90-second explanation and self-assessment 2.

Week 15 (14 December 2026): Final group video (5–8 minutes), visual-aid explanation and two questions. Use at least two news sources; submit the annotated outline and full script.

Week 16 (21–27 December 2026): Final submission of the video, annotated outline and full script; file-access checks. Submission period only.
scorePolicy:
Percentages of the final semester grade:
Midterm assessment: 24%
Coursework: 12%
  speaking tasks: 4%
  writing tasks: 4%
  Attendance: 4%
Final assessment: 24%
  group video, spoken presentation and Q & A: 12%
  annotated outline and full script: 12%
Cool English independent learning, Weeks 17–18: 20%
University common English examination: 20%
Total: 100%.

Speaking: 4% coursework (AI X-Ray, chart descriptions and recordings) plus 12% final video, spoken explanation and Q & A. Writing: 4% coursework (short writing and the personal-data writing/revision cycle) plus 12% final annotated outline and full script. Speaking and writing each account for at least 16%; the midterm essay has its separate 24% allocation.

Skill evidence: at least three assessed speaking outputs and two writing outputs, including revision after feedback, drawn from the scheduled course tasks.
Speaking criteria: Content and Task Fulfillment; Organization and Coherence; Language Use; Delivery and Fluency; Interaction and Response.
Writing criteria: Content and Task Fulfillment; Organization and Coherence; Language Use; Genre and Professional Appropriacy; Revision and Development.
Assessments use the official four-level descriptors. At least one speaking assessment covers all five dimensions; interaction is marked N/A when inapplicable to another task.

Graded tasks within each coursework skill component are averaged equally. A draft and its revision count as one writing task. Midterm and final components are counted separately. Attendance begins at 100: the first three absences have no deduction, then five attendance points are deducted per additional absence. Approved leave follows university rules.

【BESTEP 與英語能力認列】

BESTEP Speaking and Writing: 17 October 2026.
BESTEP Listening and Reading: 21 November 2026.
University common English examination: 3 November 2026, 10:10–11:25; separate 20% semester component.

Actual BESTEP participation earns 10 bonus points; an eligible other English proficiency test earns 5. Submit the required evidence by the end of the semester. Each score report is counted once, and the semester grade is capped at 100.

A verified B2 speaking or writing result may satisfy the designated 10 percentage points for that skill. The remaining 2 points in a 12-point allocation, or 6 in a 16-point allocation, are assessed through course work. Students continue to participate in the learning activities and complete the other requirements.
materials:
Main textbook: Sean Kenny, Eric Sabatino and Jacalyn Bondar, Capstone: English for Information and New Technology, Crane Publishing. Selected Units 1–3 before the midterm. Second-half selected readings and exercises: Unit 3 Robotics review; Unit 4 Hackers and Internet Security; Unit 6 DNA Testing and Family History.
Writing reference: Joseph M. Williams and Joseph Bizup, Style: Lessons in Clarity and Grace, 11th edition, selected Lessons 1–3 and accompanying exercises.
BESTEP materials: EAP Power Up: Synthesizing Textual and Visual Information for Academic Success, Language Training & Testing Center (LTTC), 2024; selected activities in reading, summarising and explaining visual information.
Additional materials: instructor-prepared slides, task sheets and assessment rubrics; cited news/data sources; Cool English online exercises.
延伸教學與資源: ● 混成學習 (Blended Learning) 課程結合實體授課與線上學習（同步視訊／非同步活動）。Combines face-to-face instruction with online learning (including synchronous video sessions or asynchronous activities).● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching) 強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.● 數位教材資源應用 (Application of Digital Resources) 採用影音多媒體或具開放授權之資源（如 OCW、開放教科書）作為主要或輔助教材。Adopts multimedia or open-licensed resources (e.g., OCW, Open Textbooks) as primary or supplementary teaching materials.● 數位科技融入 (Digital Technology Integration) 運用生成式 AI、VR/AR、IoT、IRS 等新興科技輔助教學與評量。Utilizes emerging technologies such as Generative AI, VR/AR, IoT, and IRS (Interactive Response Systems) to facilitate teaching and assessment.
課程是否導入AI: ● 使用生成式 AI 作為教學過程的輔助工具（Use generative AI tools as an aid to the teaching process）● 鼓勵學生使用生成式 AI 工具（Encourage students to use generative AI tools）● 使用生成式 AI 進行課堂即時互動（Use generative AI for real-time classroom interaction）● 簡單介紹 AI 的基本概念（Briefly introduce the basic concept of AI）
remarks: 本課程為專業英文（ESP / EAP）課程，教材、講義及簡報均採全英文；課堂授課及師生互動之英語使用比例 90% (含) 以上。
